item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, slightly positive on formal macro/fiscal and investment-rule setting, but weakened by opaque political finance and post-election patronage-style spending.

**Accepted Claims**
- [India budget shifts spending priorities while keeping fiscal deficit in check](https://theprint.in/india/india-budget-shifts-spending-priorities-while-keeping-fiscal-deficit-in-check/2187377/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 23 Jul 2024 | The government cut the fiscal-deficit target to 4.9% of GDP while raising capital and investment-linked spending, which supports a pro-rules, pro-investment reading. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.3`, `5B.1`.

- [India budget keeps spending in check, sees modest increase in revenue](https://theprint.in/india/indias-budget-keeps-spending-in-check-sees-modest-increase-in-revenue/1949061/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 1 Feb 2024 | The interim budget stayed fiscally tight despite election pressure and avoided a classic giveaway budget, which is evidence for rule-based fiscal management rather than pure vote-buying. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.3`, `5B.1`.

- [India eyes $100 billion annual foreign direct investment in coming years - IT minister](https://theprint.in/india/india-eyes-100-billion-annual-foreign-direct-investment-in-coming-years-it-minister/1928045/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 17 Jan 2024 | The government publicly framed 2024 around attracting large-scale FDI through infrastructure, manufacturing, and easier business processes, which is direct evidence of intent to improve long-run investment conditions. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.1`.

- [Moody’s raises India’s growth forecasts, Fitch affirms rating](https://theprint.in/economy/moodys-raises-indias-growth-forecasts-fitch-affirms-rating/2243897/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 29 Aug 2024 | Moody’s and Fitch cited policy continuity, strong growth, and improving inflation expectations, which is supportive evidence that the macro and investment environment remained credible to outside observers. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.3`.

- [India’s Modi chasing reform legacy shifts income goals for struggling farmers](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/indias-modi-chasing-reform-legacy-shifts-income-goals-for-struggling-farmers) | Reuters via The Straits Times | 8 May 2024 | Modi’s administration set targets to lift rural incomes, expand non-farm jobs, and increase agricultural investment, which supports a broad-based jobs-and-enterprise agenda rather than a purely extractive one. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.1`.

- [Indian government appoints members for new finance panel](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/indian-government-appoints-members-for-new-finance-panel-3287402) | Reuters via Investing.com | 30 Jan 2024 | The government named a technocratic Finance Commission team including experienced officials and economists, which is positive evidence that economic rule-setting was routed through professional institutions. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.2`.

- [Modi’s government appoints career bureaucrat as RBI governor](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=59281) | Reserve Bank of India | 11 Dec 2024 | The appointment of Sanjay Malhotra, a career IAS officer with finance and revenue experience, is technocratic evidence that the state still used senior professional administrators for core economic institutions. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.2`, `5B.3`.

- [Explainer: What were India’s electoral bonds and how did they power Modi’s party?](https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 16 Feb 2024 | Reuters described the electoral-bonds scheme as allowing unlimited anonymous donations, with the BJP the largest beneficiary, which is strong counterevidence to fair political-economic rules and clean competition. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.1`.

- [Obscure trust links India’s top businesses with Modi’s election war chest](https://theprint.in/india/obscure-trust-links-indias-top-businesses-with-modis-election-war-chest-2/2038095/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 12 Apr 2024 | A major electoral trust routed roughly 75% of its donations to the BJP, suggesting opaque business-political entanglement rather than neutral competition. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.1`.

- [Qwik, a top buyer of Indian electoral bonds, is affiliated to Ambani’s Reliance, filings show](https://theprint.in/india/qwik-a-top-buyer-of-indian-electoral-bonds-is-affiliated-to-ambani-s-reliance-filings-show/2002426/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 15 Mar 2024 | Reuters reported a Reliance-linked company bought large volumes of electoral bonds, reinforcing rent-seeking and quid-pro-quo concerns around business and political access. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.1`.

- [India’s Modi spends billions on jobs, key allies in first budget after election](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 23 Jul 2024 | The first post-election budget funneled large sums to jobs, rural programs, and coalition-partner states explicitly to win back voters and retain support, which is counterevidence that policy was insulated from short-term politics. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.1`, `5B.3`.

- [India’s Modi faces delicate balancing act in post-election budget](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-faces-delicate-balancing-act-in-post-election-budget/2186495/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 23 Jul 2024 | Reuters described the budget as balancing fiscal prudence with voter anger and coalition demands, which supports a mixed reading: rules-based budgeting remained, but political bargaining heavily shaped the outcome. IDs: `5B.4`; also `5B.3`, `5B.1`.

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence on fiscal rules, investment signals, and political finance, but little direct 2024 evidence on sector-by-sector property-rights reform or competition policy enforcement.
- The cleanest positive evidence is mostly about macro discipline and investment intent; the strongest negative evidence is about opaque funding and politically driven spending, not formal expropriation or industrial favoritism.
